clean_story:
Self-adjusting behavior. Dynamic responses.

The term adaptive systems comes from their ability to change based on conditions, like a thermostat switching a heater on or off to keep a room at 20 Celsius.

Most people think of them as smart tools, but their power lies in constant feedback. A self-driving car’s sensors detect a pedestrian crossing and brake instantly, recalculating its path 20 times per second. An email spam filter learns from every flagged message, refining its rules without human input. These systems don’t just react—they evolve, using data to fine-tune their actions over time. The precision comes from algorithms that weigh thousands of variables, like a chef adjusting a recipe after each taste test.

Three related subjects are machine learning, control theory and emergent behavior.
